subtasks.title: Guard ClarityScoutShiftController::end() against force-login impersonators (early return)
subtasks.approach:
Copy-and-adapt the shipped DEV-2232 guard from status() (same file, lines 62-70) into end(). Insert `if ($user->isScoutForceImpersonator()) { return response()->json([...]); }` AFTER the `if (! $kit)` 403 block (ends ~line 111) and BEFORE the unconditional `Analytics::track(ScoutAnalyticsEvent::ShiftEnd->value, ...)` at line 115. Returning before the Analytics call and before the DB::connection('platform')->transaction() suppresses, by construction: the ShiftEnd analytics event, the EnsureOpenShift::forKit() lazy zero-activity kit_shifts create, the close write, the SendEndOfShiftSummary dispatch, and the 'Scout shift ended' activity_log row. The payload is end()'s OWN key set with nulled values plus newly_closed:false (NOT status()'s 5-key payload) — per the Phase 2 answer, because end() responses are structurally expected to carry newly_closed. DO NOT extract a shared private helper for the duplicated predicate block: prep notes[] records that the shipped status() precedent did not extract one, and CLAUDE.md says follow the existing pattern; the literal duplication is intentional and must be called out in the PR body. Also refresh the class docblock (lines 23-34): the 'Both endpoints lazily materialize an open kit_shifts row via {@see EnsureOpenShift}' sentence is now wrong for end() too, and status()'s own docblock already documents its impersonator exception — add the matching one-line exception to the class-level block. Keep it terse (CLAUDE.md: 'Keep comments and docblocks minimal'; boost guidelines: PHPDoc over inline comments, no inline comments unless genuinely complex). Style: explicit `: JsonResponse` return type is already present; do not add new inline comments inside end().

TEST CLASS FACTS (read verbatim from tests/Feature/Http/Controllers/Api/ClarityScoutShiftControllerTest.php): `class ClarityScoutShiftControllerTest extends Tests\TestCase` — NO class-level attributes, NO traits declared in the class body, and NO `RequiresClickhouse` token anywhere in the file. It is therefore NOT CH-gated and will run in normal CI; the new test goes in this file. Test-method convention in THIS file is the `#[Test]` attribute (PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Test) over a descriptive snake_case method name with `: void` — NOT a `test_` prefix, and this file uses NO `#[Group]` attributes. setUp() builds $this->user/$this->kit/$this->token and installs a PERMISSIVE `Analytics::shouldReceive('track')->zeroOrMoreTimes()->andReturnNull()`; you CANNOT assert 'never tracked' against that. Use the file's own precedent instead: `$spy = \Mockery::spy(AnalyticsService::class); Analytics::swap($spy); ... $spy->shouldNotHaveReceived('track');` (see status_does_not_open_a_shift_or_track_shift_start_for_a_force_login_impersonator, lines 227-258 — the direct sibling to write against). Mint the force token exactly as that test does: `$this->user->createToken('clarity-scout-force-token', ['*', 'clarity-scout-force'])->plainTextToken`.

NEW TEST (one #[Test] method, sibling-named, e.g. end_does_not_close_a_shift_or_track_shift_end_for_a_force_login_impersonator): Queue::fake(); swap the Analytics spy; POST /api/scout/shift/end with the force-token Bearer header; assert 200; assert the full impersonator key set is present via assertJsonStructure(['data' => ['shift_id','open','started_at','ended_at','end_type','newly_closed']]) plus assertJsonPath('data.shift_id', null) / ('data.open', false) / ('data.newly_closed', false); assertDatabaseCount('kit_shifts', 0); $spy->shouldNotHaveReceived('track'); assert 0 Activity rows with log_name 'scout-shift' and description 'Scout shift ended'; Queue::assertNotPushed(SendEndOfShiftSummary::class). Queue and SendEndOfShiftSummary are already imported in this file. NOTE the existing status_and_end_response_shapes_are_locked test uses a NORMAL scout token, so it does NOT pin the impersonator payload — the new test must assert that key set itself. Leave every existing end() test untouched (they prove the normal-driver path is unchanged).

BLAST RADIUS: none. ClarityScoutShiftController matches no sensitive glob (not a migration, not billing, not Shield/Policy/auth config, not a ClickHouse purge/cleanup, not PruneScans).

subtasks.title: Gate ONLY the Logout analytics call in ClarityScoutAuthController::logout() — token revocation must still run
subtasks.approach:
THIS GUARD IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE FROM t1 ON PURPOSE. logout() must NOT early-return. `$request->user()->currentAccessToken()->delete()` is how an impersonating admin exits impersonation; an early return would strand them holding a live clarity-scout-force token. Only the `Analytics::track(ScoutAnalyticsEvent::Logout->value, ...)` call is gated. Ordering is load-bearing: isScoutForceImpersonator() reads `currentAccessToken()?->abilities` (app/Models/User.php:252), so the predicate MUST be evaluated BEFORE the token delete — after the delete, currentAccessToken() no longer reflects a live row and the guard would misbehave. Resolve `$user = $request->user()` once at the top (the method currently calls $request->user() twice), then:

    if (! $user->isScoutForceImpersonator()) { Analytics::track(...); }
    $user->currentAccessToken()->delete();

Do not restructure anything else in the method; the success JSON body is unchanged. Boost guidelines: explicit `: JsonResponse` return type already present; no inline comment needed — if a reader needs the 'why', it belongs in the PR body and (post-approval) the wiki, per CLAUDE.md's comment-minimalism rule.

BLAST-RADIUS JUDGEMENT CALL (explicit, as required): I AM TAGGING this node `auth`. Justification: although the sensitive glob 'Shield/Policies/auth config' literally means config and policy files rather than a controller, this node's ONLY realistic failure mode is an authentication-session outcome, not an analytics one — implementing it as an early return (the shape t1 uses, and the shape a reviewer pattern-matching on t1 would reach for) leaves an admin's `clarity-scout-force` token alive and the admin stuck inside a driver's session. That is a privilege-exit failure, which is exactly the class of risk the approval gate exists for; tagging is not casual here and under-tagging to dodge the gate would be the wrong call. The tag forces one human approval line before t2 is implemented.

TEST CLASS FACTS (read verbatim from tests/Feature/Http/Controllers/Api/ClarityScoutAuthControllerTest.php): `class ClarityScoutAuthControllerTest extends Tests\TestCase` — NO class-level attributes, NO traits declared in the class body, and NO `RequiresClickhouse` token anywhere in the file. NOT CH-gated; it runs in normal CI, so the new tests go in this file. Test-method convention in THIS file differs from t1's file: methods are `test_`-PREFIXED snake_case with `: void`, each carrying `#[Group('controllers')]` and `#[Group('clarity-scout')]` — there is NO `#[Test]` attribute anywhere in this file. Match the host file, not t1. setUp() installs the same permissive `Analytics::shouldReceive('track')->zeroOrMoreTimes()->andReturnNull()`, so a 'never tracked' assertion needs the Mockery spy swap — and this file does NOT yet import App\Services\Analytics\AnalyticsService, so that import must be ADDED. Setup helper is the file-private `createScannerUser(array $userAttrs = []): User` (line 430). Force tokens are minted in this file as `$user->createToken('clarity-scout-token', ['*', 'clarity-scout-force'])->plainTextToken` (lines 211, 322, 361) and requests use `$this->withToken($token)`.

NEW TESTS (two methods, both `test_`-prefixed with both #[Group] attributes):
1. test_logout_does_not_track_logout_for_a_force_login_impersonator_but_still_revokes_the_token — swap in `$spy = \Mockery::spy(AnalyticsService::class); Analytics::swap($spy);`, createScannerUser(), mint a ['*','clarity-scout-force'] token, POST /api/scout/logout via withToken(), assertSuccessful(), `$spy->shouldNotHaveReceived('track')`, AND — the load-bearing half — assertDatabaseMissing('personal_access_tokens', ['tokenable_id' => $user->id, 'tokenable_type' => $user->getMorphClass()]) exactly as the existing test_can_logout does. Without that revocation assertion an early-return implementation would pass.
2. test_logout_still_tracks_logout_for_a_normal_driver — same spy swap, a plain 'clarity-scout-token' (no force ability), POST logout, assertSuccessful(), and `$spy->shouldHaveReceived('track')->withArgs(fn (...$args): bool => ($args[0] ?? null) === ScoutAnalyticsEvent::Logout->value)->once();` — this requires ADDING the `App\Enums\ScoutAnalyticsEvent` import too (not currently imported in this file). Leave the existing test_can_logout untouched.
